cards.title: Hour 14 concentrated 67% of all weekly errors
cards.detail: Hour 14 saw 1,460 errors out of 9,225 requests, versus a steady 31 errors per hour in every other hour. This single hour accounts for 1,460 of the 2,169 total errors across the week.

cards.title: model-epsilon is failing 100% of requests
cards.detail: model-epsilon returned errors on all 40 of its 40 requests with zero spend, indicating the model is completely broken or misconfigured and should be disabled or investigated.

cards.title: caller-01 drives over half of all traffic and spend
cards.detail: caller-01 made 105,832 requests (51.6% of 204,993 total) and spent $1,643.86 (49.0% of $3,354.82), making it the dominant consumer by a wide margin. It also produced 952 errors (43.9% of all errors).

cards.title: caller-07 costs 9.5x more per request than the largest caller
cards.detail: caller-07 spent $174.12 on 1,180 requests, or $0.148 per request, compared to caller-01 at $0.0155 per request. Its cache hit rate of 0.04 is among the lowest, suggesting caching improvements could reduce cost.

cards.title: Ten callers with low cache hit rates account for a quarter of spend
cards.detail: Ten callers with cache hit rates below 0.09 (callers 03, 05, 07, 09, 11, 13, 15, 17, 21, 23) together spent approximately $850 of the $3,354.82 total. Raising their cache utilization toward the 0.87 group average could materially cut cost.

cards.title: model-alpha has the highest latency and highest spend
cards.detail: model-alpha carries 86,080 requests at a p95 latency of 2,454 ms, the slowest of all models, while also accounting for $1,409.02 or 42% of total spend. Investigating whether traffic can shift to faster models like model-gamma (p95 1,310 ms) could improve both latency and cost.
